language.title: Languages
language.text: French is the official language. Fon, Yoruba, Dendi, Bariba and other languages are spoken depending on the region.

currency.title: Currency
currency.text: CFA franc (XOF), pegged to the euro at a fixed rate.

timezone.title: Time zone
timezone.text: UTC+1 all year, with no clock change.

electricity.title: Electricity
electricity.text: 220 V, 50 Hz. Type C and E sockets: bring an adapter if needed.

health.title: Health
health.text: Yellow fever vaccination is required on entry. Ask a doctor or a vaccination centre for advice before departure.

entry.title: Entering the country
entry.text: Entry requirements (visa, documents) can change: check them with a Beninese embassy or the government's official website before travelling.

holidays.title: Main public holidays
holidays.note: Muslim holidays (variable dates) and decreed holidays are not included: check the official calendar.

unesco.q: In which year were the Royal Palaces of Abomey inscribed on UNESCO's World Heritage List?

exile.q: Which king of Dahomey surrendered in 1894 before being exiled to Martinique?
exile.exp: Béhanzin, exiled to Martinique and then Algeria.

jan10.q: What is January 10 dedicated to in Benin?
jan10.exp: It is the Day of Indigenous Religions, also called the vodun festival.

gate.q: Which town is home to the Door of No Return?
gate.exp: Ouidah, at the end of the Slave Route.

capital.q: What is the official capital of Benin?
capital.exp: Porto-Novo is the official capital; Cotonou concentrates the government and economic activity.

bronze.q: Which technique is used to cast bronze in Beninese craftsmanship?
bronze.exp: Lost wax: the object is modelled in wax, covered in clay, then the metal replaces the wax.

rename.q: In which year did Dahomey officially become Benin?

currency.q: Which currency is used in Benin?
currency.exp: The CFA franc (XOF), pegged to the euro at a fixed rate.

gelede.q: Whom do the Gelede masks honour?
gelede.exp: The Gelede honour mothers and their spiritual power.

fort.q: The fort of São João Baptista de Ajudá in Ouidah was founded by Portugal in…
fort.exp: In 1721. It now houses the Ouidah History Museum.
